steps.title: Primary Elections and Caucuses
steps.description: Each state holds primary elections or caucuses where registered party members vote for their preferred presidential candidate. Delegates are awarded proportionally or on a winner-take-all basis depending on state and party rules.
steps.description_beginner: Each state holds a vote where people pick who they want their party's candidate to be for president.
steps.did_you_know: Iowa has traditionally held the first caucus, but in 2024, South Carolina became the first Democratic primary.

steps.title: National Conventions
steps.description: Each major party holds a national convention where delegates formally nominate the presidential and vice-presidential candidates. The party platform is also adopted at the convention.
steps.description_beginner: Each party holds a big meeting to officially choose their candidate for president and decide what issues they care about.
steps.did_you_know: The first televised national convention was in 1952, and it dramatically changed how campaigns reached voters.

steps.title: General Election Campaign
steps.description: Nominated candidates from both parties campaign nationwide through debates, rallies, advertisements, and ground operations, focusing heavily on swing states.
steps.description_beginner: The chosen candidates travel around the country trying to convince people to vote for them, with debates and ads.
steps.did_you_know: The first presidential debate was between Kennedy and Nixon in 1960. Radio listeners thought Nixon won, but TV viewers favored Kennedy.

steps.title: Election Day
steps.description: Voters cast ballots at polling places or through early/mail-in voting. The popular vote in each state determines which candidate receives that state's electoral votes.
steps.description_beginner: People go to voting places or mail in their ballots to pick the president. Each state counts its votes separately.
steps.duration: First Tuesday after the first Monday in November
steps.did_you_know: Election Day was set on a Tuesday in 1845 because farmers needed a day to travel to polling places and Wednesday was market day.

steps.title: Electoral College Vote
steps.description: Electors from each state formally cast their electoral votes in December. A candidate needs 270 out of 538 electoral votes to win the presidency.
steps.description_beginner: Special representatives from each state officially vote for president in December. A candidate needs 270 votes to win.
steps.duration: First Monday after the second Wednesday in December
steps.did_you_know: There have been 165 instances of faithless electors in US history, though none have ever changed the outcome of an election.

steps.title: Inauguration
steps.description: The president-elect is sworn into office on January 20th at the U.S. Capitol. The oath of office is administered by the Chief Justice of the Supreme Court.
steps.description_beginner: The new president takes an oath and officially starts the job on January 20th at a big ceremony in Washington, D.C.
steps.responsible_party: Joint Congressional Committee on Inaugural Ceremonies
steps.did_you_know: The longest inaugural address was by William Henry Harrison in 1841 at 8,445 words. He died 31 days later from pneumonia.

roles.name: Federal Election Commission
roles.description: Independent regulatory agency that enforces campaign finance laws in federal elections.

roles.name: Secretary of State
roles.description: The chief election official in most states, responsible for overseeing election administration.

roles.name: Electoral College
roles.description: The body of 538 electors who formally elect the president and vice president.

key_terms.definition: A body of 538 electors who formally elect the president. Each state gets electors equal to its congressional delegation.

quiz.question: How many electoral votes are needed to win the US presidency?
quiz.explanation: A candidate needs 270 out of 538 electoral votes to win the presidency.

quiz.question: When is US Election Day?
options: First Tuesday after the first Monday in November
quiz.explanation: Election Day falls on the first Tuesday after the first Monday in November.

quiz.question: What is a caucus?
options: A local party meeting to select candidates
quiz.explanation: A caucus is a local meeting where party members gather to discuss and vote on candidates.

quiz.question: Who administers the presidential oath?
quiz.explanation: The Chief Justice of the Supreme Court administers the presidential oath of office.

quiz.question: What is a Super PAC?
quiz.explanation: A Super PAC can raise unlimited funds for political ads but cannot coordinate with candidates.
